                            Message from the Chairman




    Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Govt. Model College (PDUGMC), Katlicherra, Hailakandi
    was established in 2020 by the Government of Assam. It is indeed a great move to
    educate and enlighten the students belonging to rural and educationally backward
    areas. It is expected that this college will make an effort to focus on imparting
    knowledge and skill-based education. Let us strive for all round development and success
    for Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Govt. Model College, Katlicherra, Hailakandi in the
    future.

    The Governing Body of the college has als0 been constantly working to ensure the quality
    and job-oriented education in this college.

    I wish all of the students and faculty members the best of luck in their endeavors to dispel
    the darkness of ignorance and enlighten our society with sparks of knowledge and fire of
    wisdom.

    As the president of this institution, I expect full participation, coordination and
    cooperation from students and parents in order to make those dreams a reality. Please
    feel free to contact me if you feel necessary, whether for personal or professional
    reasons.

    I wish you the best of luck!

                             From the Principal’s Desk




    The establishment of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Govt. Model College, Katlicherra,
    Hailakandi by the RUSA and the Government of Assam in 2020 is a matter of pride for
    the people of Katlicherra in particular, and the Hailakandi District in general. It is a
    dream project of the Assam government, funded by the Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha
    Abhiyan (RUSA). The college came into being as a result of the continuous efforts of the
    Department of Higher Education, Govt. of Assam and the RUSA, Assam, and the college
    has finally been able to open its doors to the first batch of students for the academic year
    2020-2021. We successfully completed our first academic session with the help of all
    college stakeholders. Initially, the college's goals were limited to providing education in
    the Arts stream only.

    I am pleased to announce that the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Govt. Model College,
    Katlicherra will admit its second batch of students for the academic session 2021-2022
    for Higher Secondary 1st Year Arts and B.A. 1st Semester classes. The goal of the
    government initiative to establish the college was to provide high-quality competitive
    higher education comparable to that available in the country's best institutes, with a
    focus on arts education that is affordable and accessible to all sections of the community.

    The permanent campus of the College, is likely to be established at Sultanicherra, the
    southern part of Hailakandi District. Sultani Village/ Sultanicherra, is situated 43 km
    away from district headquarter Hailakandi and is located in Katlichara Tehsil of
    Hailakandi district in Assam. The college's temporary campus is conveniently located at
    Unused building (Girls’ Hostel and MSDP Building) of Jamira High School, Jamira
    Bazar, near national highway 154. Which is at a short distance of about 3.5 kms from the
    original venue Sultanicherra and about 47 km away from district headquarter,
    Hailakandi.


                                                [2]
 3

    Despite the fact that the college's infrastructure has not yet been constructed, we do not
    want to keep the students of this region waiting any longer. We expect to complete all of
    the construction work within a year or two. Meanwhile, I'd like to invite all deserving
    students from the region to enroll in this college and become a part of this historic
    initiative, as well as participate in our progress toward excellence.

    The College offers Higher Secondary courses (10+2) in Arts Stream under Assam Higher
    Secondary Education Council, Guwahati, as well as Bachelor of Arts course under Assam
    University, Silchar. The College is affiliated to Assam University, Silchar from the
    academic session 2020-2021. Very soon, the College will get permission from Assam
    Higher Secondary Education Council, Guwahati.

    A slew of highly qualified and dedicated faculty members will make every effort to
    impart education while also monitoring students on a regular basis for overall
    improvement. I consider myself very fortunate to be able to inform you that we have
    well-qualified and energetic teachers who are enthusiastic about their profession. I hope
    that our students will be able to excel in their academic and intellectual pursuits as a
    result of their participation in this institution.

    The majority of the villagers who live near the college are both educationally and
    financially disadvantaged. Despite the fact that there are many Middle & High schools in
    and around the area, opportunities to pursue higher education are limited.

    I am delighted to be taking over the reins of this new college. I hope, or rather, know,
    that we will achieve and set many milestones in the coming years with the help of
    dedicated staff and the assistance of local residents, whose intellectual and general
    growth is our primary focus.

    `I welcome you to the prestigious institution of higher learning, assuring you of a
    nurturing and caring environment, with the expectation that this institution will provide
    you with all means of material and intellectual gratification and will assist you in
    pursuing and achieving your goals.




    Dr. S.R. Barbhuiya

         Principal

                                COLLEGE PROFILE
    1. About the College
       The establishment of the Model Degree College is a part of the proactive measures undertaken
    by the Government of India to expand higher educational facilities and ensure that all states in the
    country meet the national average of Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) in higher education. To fulfill
    this, the Central Government has launched an important scheme- “Scheme for Financing New
    Model Colleges in Educationally Backward Districts (EBDs)”, which is essentially a motivational
    mechanism for state governments to improve educational outcomes in underserved districts by
    providing appropriate financial assistance. Under this scheme Government of Assam established
    five Model Degree Colleges in the year 2017, and all these Model Degree Colleges were named
    after Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya, a great thinker, philosopher, sociologist and politician of the
    country. The Government of Assam, in its second phase, established six new Govt. Model Degree
    Colleges in the year 2020, which were later renamed as Govt. Model College. Pandit Deendayal
    Upadhyaya, Govt. Model College, Katlicherra is one of these six newly established Government
    Model Colleges.
        Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Government Model College, Katlicherra, Hailakandi was
    proposed to be built at Sultanicherra Garden under South Hailakandi Constituency, which is about
    48 km far from Hailakandi, the district headquarter and 33 km from Lala town. The transport and
    communication facilities of the area are adequately developed, and the college is well connected to
    district headquarter and other parts of the Hailakandi district. Although the permanent building of
    the college is yet to be constructed, it starts functioning profusely at a temporary venue located in
    Jamira High School Campus. The majority of the villagers residing around the college are
    educationally and finically backward. The college is a blazing light in this educationally backward
    and interior region which will empower and enlighten the learners. It being the only college, the
    ambitious students can see a ray of hope to pursue higher studies which was earlier a dream they
    cherished. Now they can mould their future in this holy shrine of learning. The College has started
    its journey only with faculty of Arts comprising of eight departments viz, English, Bengali,
    Economics, Political Science, History, Geography, Education and Mathematics. The college has
    opened its doors for the first batch of students from the academic session 2020-21. After
    successfully completing the third academic session, the college has started its admission process for
    Higher Secondary 1st Year (Arts) and B.A. 1st Semester for the academic session 2024-25.

    At present, the college is offering Higher Secondary Course in arts stream under Assam Higher
    Secondary Education Council (AHSEC) and four year under-graduate programme in accordance
    with NEP 2020 under Assam University, Silchar. The aim of the college is to impart quality higher
    education and prepare the students for their secure future and noble humanitarian cause, thereby
    contributing much to society. As it is a Government Model College, each and every classroom and
    department is well-equipped with modern advanced technologies, and students are being taught by
    a galaxy of highly qualified and dedicated faculty members who are putting their best efforts to
    impart quality education along with continuous monitoring of students for their overall
    improvement.

                  TWO YEARS HIGHER SECONDARY COURSE
    The Two-Year Higher Secondary Course is administered according to the regulations set forth by
    the Assam Higher Secondary Education Council (AHSEC). This course spans two academic years:
    the First Year and the Second Year, also known as the Final Year. Admission to the HS course
    commences promptly following the announcement of the HSLC Examination results by the Board
    of Secondary Education, Assam (SEBA). The admission schedule is publicized in alignment with
    the notifications issued by the Assam Higher Secondary Education Council. It is noteworthy that
    the admission process is facilitated through the Darpan portal.

    2. ELIGIBILITY

    For seeking admission to the First Year of Higher Secondary Course, a candidate must have passed
    H.S.L.C. Examination of Board of Secondary Education (SEBA) or Secondary Examination of
    CBSE or other Boards examination recognised by Assam Higher Secondary Education Council
    (AHSEC). Candidates other than SEBA will have to produce Migration Certificate in due time, else
    their candidature will be cancelled. Admission in H.S. Course will be given strictly on the basis of
    merit, and Admission Committee will finalise the list of candidates for admission. There is a
    provision for reservation of seats for students belonging to SC, ST, OBC, MOBC, PWD, etc. Any
    break in studies after passing HSLC or equivalent examination must be supported by a GAP’
    Certificate issued as per specified proforma by an appropriate authority.

    3. COURSE-CURRICULA

    The course and curricula of H.S. are conducted as per the rules and regulations of the Assam
    Higher Secondary Education Council (AHSEC). Students seeking admission in HS First Year will
    have three core subjects and can choose four elective subjects from the list given below, of which

    5. EXAMINATIONS
    The Course comprises two examinations viz. i) First Year and ii) Second Year or Final Year.
    Promotion to Second Year or Final Year depends on the successful completion of the first-year
    examination conducted under the guidelines of Assam Higher Secondary Education Council,
    Guwahati. The unsuccessful candidates in H.S. first year and H.S. second year may re-appear as per
    rules of AHSEC at the next final examination as non-collegiate candidate.

    A. FYUG
    ❖ DEGREE PROGRAMME OFFERED
    The Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUG) at Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Govt. Model
    College, Katlicherra, is affiliated with Assam University, Silchar, and as such, is governed by the
    rules and regulations of the University. The FYUG course is divided into eight semesters with
    internal examinations/assignments/seminars and an end- semester examination in each semester.
    The University conducts all the semester examinations, and after satisfactory performances in all
    the semesters, a candidate will be awarded the final degree on the basis of a composite score in all
    the semesters.
    ❖ PROGRAMME OF STUDYUNDER FYUG
    The institution provides a Four-Year Undergraduate (FYUG) Course under the National Education
    Policy 2020. The duration of FYUG is four years, and each year consists of two semesters each of
    six months’ duration. However, the course is divided into four parts:
    i. Certificate is awarded for successfully completing on one year course.
    ii. Diploma is awarded for successfully completing two years course.
    iii. Bachelor’s Degree is awarded for successfully completing a three-year course.
    iv. Bachelor’s Degree with Honours is awarded for successfully completing four years
    Note: Entry and exit in the course is open so a student can leave the institution after completing
    one, two, or three years and rejoin to complete the remaining course with in the student’s life cycle
    of 7 years.

    Note: Maximum duration for the completion of a FYUG program of study is 7 (seven) years at a
    stretch from the date of admission (i.e, 10 (ten) consecutive End Semester Examinations) as per the
    “Guidelines on Determination of a Uniform Span Period within which a student may be allowed to
    Qualify for a Degree” published by UGC dated October 15, 2015. This criterion shall be strictly
    adhered to while determining the eligibility to appear in any ESE for Arrear Paper/s, and
    Betterment Examination.

      not less than three academic years and successfully completes all the examinations of all six
      semesters prescribed for the program. A candidate is eligible for the award of degree in FYUG, on

     ❖ CLASS ATTENDANCE
        Class attendance percentage of each subject in each semester shall be calculated on the basis of
        total class attended percent number of classes held in the semester. A student with less than 75 per
        cent of attendance on a paper shall not be allowed to appear in the end semester examination in the
        particular subject. However, the student can take admission in the next semester and appear in the
        similar examinations if he/she has secured the passing marks in the previous semesters; otherwise,
        they have to reappear in the sessional test in the concern paper. If the student secured passing
        marks in all the sessional test in the previous semesters, then the internal marks would be carried

     B. ADMISSION PROCESS IN FYUG
     ❖ Guidelines Under CUET/NON-CUET
     In PDU Govt. Model College, Katlicherra, a student can take admission both through CUET and
     Non-CUET mode. A student must mention whether he/she has applied for CUET during the
     registration process along with other details.
     ❖ Academic Bank of Credits
     Academic Bank of Credits has been established on the lines of the National Academic Depository
     (NAD), in the sense, NAD is the backbone of ABC, where the students' academic data are held and
     academic awards are stored (i.e. storehouse of academic awards). Despite the fact that ABC enables
     students to register or commence credit transfer, the final outcomes of credit redemption and
     issuance of certificates, as well as the compilation of award records, are administered by academic
     institutions via the NAD Platform. Hence being the owner of academic awards, Academic
     Institutions must mandatorily register themselves under ABC via NAD. Before enrolling in FYUG
     courses, students have to register their name in the Academic Bank of Credit
     (https://www.abc.gov.in) using their Aadhaar number and registered mobile number.
     ❖ Samarth Admission Portal

     registration in the admission portal. Later the students can choose the colleges and universities they

     C. GUIDELINES FOR FYUG EXAMINATION
     The examination under FYUG is parted into two categories. First is internal assessment through
     Internal Examination/Assignment/Seminar/Project report along with the marks obtained in
     attendance. Second is session examination in the end of each semester. The following points are
     enumerated in respect of FYUG examinations.
     ● Marking system on percentage of attendance is same as CBCS.10marksforpaperwithout practical
       and 6 marks for paper with practical
     ● Total marks allotted for internal examination/ assignment/ seminar/ project report is 20 marks
       for papers without practical and 14 marks for papers with practical.
     ● Totalmarksallotedforpracticalexaminationis30 marks
     ● For sessional examination, total marks allotted for paper without practical is 70 marks and with
       practical is 50 marks.
     ● A student must attain the minimum marks in internal assessment in order to sit in the final
       examination. Out of 20 marks he/she has to attain 8 marks and out of 14 marks he/she has to
       attain 6 marks in internal examination/ assignment/ seminar/ project report and a minimum of
       75% in class attendance. Further, a student must attain a minimum of 12 marks out of 30 marks
       in total internal assessment.
     ● A student fails to attain the minimum marks in the internal assessment will not be allowed to sit
       in the final examination

                     INTERNAL DISCIPLINE OF THE COLLEGE

     PDU Govt. Model College, Katlicherra is committed to maintain a high standard of internal
     discipline for creating a conducive academic environment. Therefore, the students are advised to
     abide by the following guidelines:

     1. All forms of ragging are strictly banned in this college. The college is committed to follow the
       anti-ragging rules laid down by UGC in letter and spirit. If any student is found involved or
       reported to be involved in ragging, directly or indirectly, exemplary punishment will be given (to
       him/he), which may include cancellation of admission from the college, and the matter may be
       reported to the police. All selected students will have to submit an anti-ragging undertaking in
       the prescribed format at the time of admission.
     2. Writing/sticking bills and posters on the walls, spitting and littering shall be treated as breach of
       discipline. Furthermore, any damage caused to college property (including furniture, doors and
       windows, library books, sports materials) must be compensated by the concerned student.
     3. Students must maintain the decorum of the class room, examination hall and library.
     4. Use of Mobile Phones is strictly prohibited in the classroom and inside the college campus
       unless permitted by the concerned teacher/college authority.
     5. The students are expected to abide by all the rules and regulations of the college. Any violation
       of rules and regulations will invite strict disciplinary action such as cancellation of admission,
       forced transfer, non-issuing of college certificate or any other punishment deems fit by the
       college authority.
